title: Sequential Processing
definition: A method of executing a series of tasks in a specific order, with each task completed before the next one begins.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Imagine a to-do list where you have to complete one task before moving on to the next. This is like that, but for computers.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: In the context of CPU-only systems, sequential processing is necessary because CPUs can only execute one task at a time. This ensures that the second task doesn't interfere with the first one.
difficulty_levels.expert: Sequential processing is a fundamental concept in computer science. It's used in single-threaded systems to avoid race conditions and to ensure data consistency. However, it can lead to inefficiencies in systems with multi-core CPUs. Parallel processing is a potential solution, but it requires a more complex architecture.

extra_fields.insight: The fix for CPU-only systems processing tasks one at a time is to implement sequential processing with enough breathing room between tasks.
